index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the training architecture of a causality-aware condition adapter (CA²) integrated into a diffusion-based image editing framework. The global layout is divided into three main sections: on the left, two hourglass-shaped networks represent the SD Unet (blue) and Reference Net (orange), both composed of stacked rectangular blocks symbolizing neural layers; the SD Unet is marked as frozen (indicated by a snowflake icon), while the Reference Net is trainable (indicated by a flame icon). These networks are connected via bidirectional arrows, suggesting feature exchange during training. At the top-left, an input noise tensor feeds into the SD Unet, and at the bottom-left, a modified image (with darkened eyes) feeds into the Reference Net, producing an output image (Obama with open eyes) at the top-left corner.

The central and largest section, labeled 'Causality-Aware Condition Adapter', contains the core modules. It begins with a Text Encoder (red rectangle) receiving a textual prompt such as 'Open eyes', which outputs Text Tokens. These tokens are processed by a Text Cross Attention module (red rectangle) that connects to a series of 3D block-like structures representing multi-layered attention mechanisms. Concurrently, an Original Image (Obama with closed eyes) is fed into an Image Encoder (yellow rectangle), generating Image Tokens. These tokens pass through an Image Cross Attention module (yellow rectangle), which also connects to the same 3D block structure. The outputs from both cross-attention branches are combined via a matrix multiplication (M) operation, indicated by a blue circle with 'M' inside, and then undergo element-wise product operations (blue circles with '•') with a dynamic score map.

The Score Predictor (light blue rectangle) receives flattened tokens from a latent variable Z and generates a 'Score' heatmap (visualized as a blue thermal image with highlighted eye regions). This score map is subtracted from 1 (labeled '1-') and used to modulate the visual condition via element-wise multiplication. The resulting modulated visual features are then combined with the textual condition via concatenation (C) before being fed back into the 3D attention blocks. The final output is a refined image with open eyes, demonstrating the successful application of the condition.

The legend at the bottom clarifies symbols: M denotes Matrix Multiply, • denotes Element-wise Product, C denotes Concatenate, and the blue arrow indicates Visualization. Two types of condition flows are shown: textual condition (brown arrows) and visual condition (yellow arrows). The top legend defines SD Unet (blue hourglass), Reference Net (orange hourglass), Frozen (snowflake), and Trainable (flame). The caption explains that CA² injects skin details from the original image via an additional attention mechanism and uses an adaptive score map to dynamically modulate visual condition intensity, preventing conflicts in causality modeling.
